reason: The hypothesis directly restates the exact intervention, mechanism, and predicted outcomes from P1 (and related passages P5, P6, P8) for single-phase ZrB2, and applies the general concept from P19. The only new element is the proposed application to resist hole formation in a liquid plating bath, which is a minor extension of the already-demonstrated improved oxidation resistance from P1, without a new mechanism or integration of disparate findings.
copied_elements: Ultra-high pressure sintering (UHPS) of ZrB2 at ~1450 °C and 15 GPa
Plastic deformation-induced dislocation multiplication and grain boundary sliding as densification mechanism
Refined grain structure with high dislocation density
Full densification at significantly lower temperature than conventional sintering
Improved mechanical properties (hardness, flexural strength) compared to conventionally sintered ZrB2
